_comment: Supplemental pool data to extend the upstream bitcoin-data/mining-pools pools.json. Add entries here when a pool uses a coinbase signature not yet in the upstream. Also defines slug_aliases to canonicalize slugs from other data sources (e.g. bitcoin_miners_myrp.parquet) to match the canonical slug derived from pools.json name resolution.

slug_aliases._comment: Maps alternative slugs (as found in bitcoin_miners_myrp.parquet or legacy data) to canonical slugs derived from pools.json name resolution. Canonical slug = to_slug(official_name_from_pools_json).

pool_types._comment: Type overrides for slugs from upstream pools.json where we cannot add a type inline. Values: solo, pool.

supplement_overrides._comment: When bitcoin_blocks_pool.parquet resolves a block to one of these slugs (via coinbase_tag), it beats myrp's more generic attribution. Format: supplement_slug -> list of myrp slugs it overrides.

_comment_generic: generic_tags: coinbase tags that name pool software, not a pool. They label a block only when no specific tag, payout address or jlopp label does (pool_resolver.py precedence rule 4).
_comment_payout_to_miners: Pools whose coinbase pays their miners directly, so a payout address in their blocks names a miner, not a pool: their tag beats a conflicting payout address (pool_resolver.py rule 2). Solo pools (pool_types 'solo') are added automatically. Evidence: median non-OP_RETURN coinbase outputs per tagged block, heights 0-975,618: Eligius 66, ckpool.org 150, OCEAN 17, against 1 for AntPool, Foundry, F2Pool, ViaBTC (review/bdl-060). OCEAN: https://ocean.xyz/docs/tides ; Eligius: https://en.bitcoin.it/wiki/Eligius ; ckpool.org: https://ckpool.org

_comment_sub_pools: bdl-063 (2026-11-13). A sub-pool is an operator that runs its own pool service for other miners and whose name appears in the coinbase text of blocks paid to another pool, the host, whose server built them. For such a block pool = the sub-pool and host_pool = the host (pool_resolver.py); concentration is counted by host_pool. Test used for every pair: the host's own tagged blocks paid the same address in the same period (column host_same_addr_2016 in review/bdl-063/data/pair_evidence.csv (Bitcoin Data Labs chain check, tip 975,618)). Customer or worker names, software tags and AntPool & friends template sharing are not sub-pools: see tag_payout_decisions. 'note' feeds pool_facts.json identification_note.

_comment_tag_payout_decisions: bdl-063 (2026-11-13). Every other tag != payout pair, decided one at a time. label 'payout': pool = host_pool = the paid pool (the text is a customer or worker name, a template-sharing artefact, or a source conflict). label 'tag': pool = host_pool = the pool named in the text (the pool pays its miners in the coinbase, or the address was handed over: the payout pool's own tagged blocks never paid it in that period). Pairs in neither section follow the default rule (payout wins, except for payout_to_miners_slugs) and are listed as undecided in data/status/tag_payout_pairs.json.

_comment_cooccurrence: bdl-063. Co-occurrence labels (method 'cooccurrence'): an unknown block gets host pool P when its first payout script is also the first payout script of at least min_identified_blocks blocks identified by tag, regex or payout, and at least min_share of those belong to host pool P. jlopp, generic and co-occurrence labels never count as evidence; scripts whose identified blocks include a payout_to_miners pool are excluded. Recomputed on every run (resolve_blocks.py); evidence in data/status/cooccurrence_scripts.json.
